adam.headline: The safest hands in the league, until a pass arrives with a defender close.
text: Adam gives the ball away 1.4 times per game and takes it back far more often: 16 forced turnovers against 8 giveaways, the best trade among the regulars. His passes go to good spots too, worth 0.80 points a shot, and 36% of them go in.
On defense he is beaten on 11% of shots, opponents shoot 19% when he stays in front, and he does it while carrying 1.30x an even share of the defending. Reilly is 2 of 12 against him.

The one habit to fix: when a pass reaches him with a defender close, he holds it, 9 of 12 times, and those shots rarely fall. Shooting on the catch or moving it on would turn a 37% TS shooter into a useful one.

zach.headline: Shoots the most, gets open the most, and needs the next one to go in.
text: Zach has taken 41 shots in 6 games, 68% of them open, and made them at 31% TS. The looks are about league average for where he takes them, so this is finishing, not shot selection.

The pressure is real: 22 forced turnovers, the most in the league, which more than covers his 19 giveaways. Viraj guarding him got beaten 5 of 12 times, but when Viraj stayed in front, Zach went 0 for 7.

Rebounding is the quiet cost: 1.0 per game once free rebounds count half, the fewest of the regulars. Across 54 results his teams win 13.7 points of win chance less than expected (17-37), the clearest signal in the league. More boards and fewer forced shots are the way out.

alex.headline: Wins the boards and gives the possessions back.
text: Alex is the best rebounder of the regulars by this count: 3.6 per game, and 2.3 once free rebounds count half.

The shots come from hard spots: 0.13 points a shot below the league, at 29% TS. When a pass reaches him in a contest he holds it every time (5 of 5), and the looks he sets up for others are worth 0.34 points a shot, the lowest here.
He gives the ball away 3.2 times per game, second only to Reilly, and that is the biggest swing available to him. On defense he is beaten a third of the time, but he held Ian to 0 for 10.

ben.headline: Nobody gets past him, and teammates keep wasting his passes.
text: Ben has never been tagged as beaten. Opponents shoot 17% when he is in position, and Adam, one of the better scorers, is 5 of 14 against him.

He scores at 49% TS while taking harder looks than most (only 45% of his shots are open), and gives the ball away 1.0 times per game, the fewest in the league. He forces only 6 turnovers, so he is a wall more than a ball hawk.

He sets up 6.0 shots per game, level with Evan for the most, but only 26% go in, and teammates held the ball first on 13 of his 19 contested set-ups. That part is on the receivers. Over 55 results his teams win 7.8 points of win chance more than expected (33-22).

g-ian.headline: Stays in front of everyone and leaves the shooting to others.
text: Ian is beaten on 9% of shots and held Alex to 4 of 20, the best single matchup on film. When opponents do shoot over him, though, they hit 40%.
His set-ups are good looks, 0.82 points a shot with 37% going in, and teammates held the ball first on 7 of his 11 contested ones.
He has taken 15 shots in 4 games at 27% TS, so scoring is not his job yet. His rebounds are hard-won, 71% of them contested. His win impact is about zero (9-7).

evan.headline: Three games, three wins, and the best looks in the league.
text: Evan scores at 58% TS on shots worth 0.38 points more than the league average, because he gets close. He gives it away 1.3 times per game and forced 11 turnovers against 4 giveaways.

He passes a lot, 6.0 set-ups per game, but into tough spots worth 0.51 points a shot. Most of his assists came from teammates holding and then making a contested shot, so his Real AST is 0.6 against 1.6.
He carries a light defensive load (0.67x) and was beaten 2 of 6 times. +29 on Win chance added and 12-4 over every result. Three filmed games is still an early read.

g-lukas.headline: Seven shots, mostly close ones, and teams that keep winning.
text: Lukas has 71% TS on the best shot quality in the league (+0.42), but on 7 shots in 3 games.
He plays off the ball, with almost no set-ups, and is rarely the tagged defender (0.39x load). When he is, the shots have gone in (beaten 2 of 5), on far too few to judge.
His teams are 11-3 over every result, +9.2 points of win chance from having him. Three filmed games is still an early read.

reilly.headline: Draws the hardest assignments and makes the best passes.
text: Reilly carries the heaviest defensive load in the league, 1.40x an even share. He is rarely beaten (13%), but opponents still hit 43% over him, which is what guarding the best scorer looks like. Adam is 1 of 8 against him when he stays in front.
His set-ups are worth 1.08 points a shot and 55% of them go in, the best passing by quality on film.

The ball is the problem: 3.4 giveaways per game, the most in the league, and only 3 forced against 9. Over 23 results his teams win 5.4 points of win chance more than expected (13-10). Three filmed games is still an early read.

viraj.headline: Gets beaten half the time, and wins the possession when he doesn't.
text: Viraj has been beaten on 8 of 16 shots, the highest rate in the league, mostly in the half court. When he stays in front, opponents shoot 25%, and Zach went 0 for 7 against him.
On offense he has 8 shots in 3 games at 25% TS, and his set-ups go to low-value spots (0.32 points a shot).
He is 0-3 on film with -28 on Win chance added, but 6-6 over every result, and his win impact is too close to call. Three filmed games is still an early read.
